Order 
1. This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 29.07.2016 passed by the Fifth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 104/2015, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Fifth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.

The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Jahar Singh in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.3,19,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

4. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellants have preferred this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4574 2 MA-180-2017 appeal on the ground that impugned award passed by the learned Tribunal is contrary to settled principles of law and evidence on record, as the Tribunal has erroneously treated the deceased Jahar Singh as an unskilled labourer and assessed his monthly income at merely 4,000/-, whereas he was a skilled marble tile artisan earning about 18,000/-
per month; further, the Tribunal committed a manifest error in deducting 50% of the income towards personal expenses despite the fact that five family members, namely his parents, brother,
Shivcharan vs Ramlakhan Kushwah on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131368484/
1 sister and grandmother, were dependent upon him, resulting in incorrect determination of loss of dependency; the compensation awarded under conventional heads such as loss of property and love and affection is grossly inadequate and does not reflect the circumstances of the case.
Hence, prayed for enhancement of compensation.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No. 3/Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation on the basis of the evidence available on record.
It is contended that the appeal lacks merit and deserves to be dismissed.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
Further, on perusal of record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the claimants have failed to adduce any substantial evidence in regard to income of the deceased.

Hence, this Court finds it appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as an unskilled person in view of the law laid down in the cases o f Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways,
2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 in which it is held that when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.

sentences.text: Therefore, in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4574 3 MA-180-2017 considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.5,845/- per month.

8. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment o f National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 40% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 18 be applied instead of 11.

sentences.text: Also, in view of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur and Others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131 , the claimants are entitled to get compensation towards loss of consortium and loss of estate.

 After deducting dependency 1/2 Rs.49098/-
Multiplier
Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 2  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-

Total Compensation = Rs.9,93,764/-

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.6,74,764/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4574 4 MA-180-2017 11.
Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.6,74,764/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
13. In view of the foregoing discussion, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of accordingly.
